I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most here in Quzhou: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land. That is the most stable way for me to use the full year, match our local water and temperature conditions, and avoid taking unnecessary market and production risk. I am 48, I do not want an overly complicated planting structure with too many small crops to manage. I would rather run a familiar wheat-maize rotation well than scatter my effort. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer moderate but steady, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and disease with a few targeted sprays. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into hybrid summer maize, because maize after wheat fits the season tightly and gives me dependable yield if I secure emergence, enough fertilizer, and a few timely irrigations. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and efficient for me between crops, and I will keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for major pests, diseases, and weeds. My goal is not maximum input, but stable output and manageable fieldwork across the whole year.
